definition: arrangements which, in a given area, make up how we know what we know (Knorr Cetina)
source_quote: Knorr Cetina's definition of epistemic cultures as "those… arrangements… which, in a given area… make up how we know what we know"

label: machineries of knowing
definition: an epistemic culture consists of three machineries: epistemic subjects, objects, and practices
source_quote: He writes that an epistemic culture consists of three "machineries of knowing": "epistemic subjects," "epistemic objects," and "epistemic practices" (Kaounas, 2024, p. 10)

label: epistemic subjects
definition: the group of people producing knowledge within an epistemic culture and their social relations
source_quote: "The machinery of epistemic subjects refers to the group of people that produce knowledge within an epistemic culture"

label: epistemic objects
definition: the collection of things with which members of an epistemic culture interact to produce knowledge
source_quote: "The machinery of epistemic objects refers to the collection of things with which the members of an epistemic culture interact to produce knowledge."

label: epistemic practices
definition: the set of patterns of action established in an epistemic culture
source_quote: "The machinery of epistemic practices… refers to the set of patterns of action that are established in an epistemic culture" (Kaounas, 2024, p. 10)

label: tacit knowledge
definition: a form of knowledge that's not shareable without the experience; understood only through the practice producing it
source_quote: there is "a form of knowledge that's not shareable without the experience" (Kaounas, 2024, p. 25)

label: circularity of artistic research
definition: knowledge production takes place through and results in artistic creation, ending where it starts
source_quote: "the knowledge production carried out by my participants not only takes place through artistic creation, but also results in artistic creation" (Kaounas, 2024, p. 28)

label: new materialist art practice as research
definition: inquiry through artistic practice where matter is active, apparatuses constitutive, knowledge emerges materially
source_quote: New materialist art practice as research is inquiry conducted in and through artistic practice under conditions in which matter is active, apparatuses are constitutive

label: data as facta
definition: data as created, produced, emerging from interactions of technological and theoretical tools (Pirrò)
source_quote: "Data might as well have a double nature of 'facta,' created, produced, and emerging from the interactions between all the technological and theoretical tools that scientists employ"

label: materialisation
definition: emerges through performance; a process of sedimentation resulting from reiteration or citation (Butler)
source_quote: “the materialisation that occurs in the interplay between the matter of bodies, cultural knowledges or discourse, and the materials of production” (Bolt, 2024, p. 271)

label: methexis
definition: Bolt's notion, developed from Carter's 'concurrent actual production' and Indigenous Australian painting
source_quote: Drawing on Paul Carter's phrase "concurrent actual production," Bolt develops her notion of methexis.

label: working hot
definition: painting as response to interactions of paint, oil, turps, canvas, gravity, sun, heat, body; causal not significatory
source_quote: Bolt names this condition of practice "working hot."

label: concurrent actual production
definition: Paul Carter's phrase, drawn on by Bolt in developing methexis
source_quote: Drawing on Paul Carter's phrase "concurrent actual production," Bolt develops her notion of methexis.

label: index (Peirce)
definition: the index retains a direct causal relation between thing and sign
source_quote: Bolt turns to Peirce's index because the index retains a "direct causal relation" between thing and sign.

label: non-unitary (nomadic) subjectivity
definition: a nomadic, dispersed, fragmented vision, nonetheless functional, coherent, accountable, embedded and embodied
source_quote: "Non-unitary subjectivity here means a nomadic, dispersed, fragmented vision, which is nonetheless functional, coherent, and accountable, mostly because it is embedded and embodied"

label: Indigenous Australian painting
definition: tradition Bolt draws from: productive rather than representative; meaning and reality constituted in performance
source_quote: Bolt draws from Indigenous Australian painting, which is productive rather than representative, where "meaning and reality are constituted in the performance" (Bolt, 2003, p. 273)

label: Jefferies

label: David Byrne
definition: musician; co-creator of My Life in the Bush of Ghosts; resists representational understanding of music

label: Stiegler

label: "Artistic Research: A Performative Paradigm?" (2016)
definition: Bolt (2016); artistic research in the shadow of science-as-research, seen as lacking credibility

definition: Mäkikoskela article on three-dimensional visual art practice, chiasm, and material resistance

label: From Hand to Mouth

label: Raw Flows (2016)

label: performative research paradigm

label: repetition with difference
definition: against scientific validity tied to repetition of the same, the performative paradigm's mode of operation

label: artistic thinking
definition: visual art practice as conceptual and analytical activity, not only practical work

label: distributed agency

label: research-creation
definition: cannot be deemed successful in simple or finite terms; opens up new fields of understanding

label: sensory ethnography
definition: an experimental iterative-inductive process with embodied sensory engagement in studio/lab environments
source_quote: It describes sensory ethnography as an "experimental iterative-inductive process" (Jefferies, 2019)

label: grammaticalization
definition: digital media's conversion of continuous material process into discrete units, vs analog real magnitudes

label: implosive writing
definition: writing method used in Becoming a Tomato's arts-based research framework

label: co-becoming
definition: process in which binary borders between human/non-human, self/other, natural/cultural are blurred

label: third space

definition: how Barad presents posthumanist performativity: an elaboration of Butler and Haraway

label: subjectivist potency
definition: specifically modern attitude or ethos in which the human subject dominates nature as agent
source_quote: yields a conceptual and practical domination of nature as well as a specifically modern attitude or ethos of subjectivist potency” (Coole & Frost, 2010, p. 9)

label: recursiveness
definition: the world as recursive, relational, non-deterministic, so the whole of logic must be reconstructed for it
source_quote: quoting Gregory Bateson's suggestion that "'the whole of logic would have to be reconstructed for recursiveness'" (Wolfe, 2010, p. xviii, citing Clarke, citing Bateson, 1972)

label: dull matter
definition: matter parsed as inert “it, things”, the figure Bennett opposes to vibrant life
source_quote: Bennett likewise opposes the parsing of the world into “dull matter (it, things)” and “vibrant life (us, beings)”

label: vibrant life
definition: life parsed as “us, beings”, the pole Bennett refuses to separate from dull matter
source_quote: Bennett likewise opposes the parsing of the world into “dull matter (it, things)” and “vibrant life (us, beings)”

label: entanglement
definition: relation in which knower, known, ethics, and apparatus are co-constituted from the start rather than separable
source_quote: “Entangled agencies” do not precede their relations; they emerge through them (Timeto, 2011, pp. 153, 164). The researcher is part of the apparatus.

label: semiotic resources
definition: Diverse resources that work together, play a collaborative role, shape each other, and can be agentive.
source_quote: Canagarajah (2018a) describes this in terms of diverse semiotic resources working together, playing “a collaborative role,” shaping “each other,” and capable of being “agentive” (p. 39).

label: event of becoming
definition: Research functioning as an event in which decisions have to be made for the moment, by the moment.
source_quote: Research “can function as an event of becoming, one in which ‘decisions have to be made for the moment, by the moment’” (Thrift, 2007, p. 217, cited in Siffrinn and Coda, 2025, p. 198).

label: theoretico-methodological experimentation
definition: The experimental research practice these theories require, given their distinct ontological commitments.
source_quote: these theories “invite more experimental research practices” and require “theoretico-methodological experimentation” (Siffrinn & Coda, 2025, pp. 191, 198).

label: boundary-making practices
definition: What apparatuses are: material-discursive practices productive of, and part of, the phenomena produced.
source_quote: her insistence that apparatuses are boundary-making practices support this shift (Barad, 2007, pp. 176, 146). For Barad, apparatuses are “specific material-discursive practices”

label: relata
definition: the terms of a relation; they do not pre-exist material-discursive arrangements but emerge within them
source_quote: relata do not preexist their relations but emerge through specific agential cuts and apparatuses (Barad, 2007, pp. 139–141, 333–334).

label: vitality
definition: capacity of things to act as quasi agents or forces with trajectories, propensities, or tendencies of their own
source_quote: defining vitality as the capacity of things not only to impede human designs but also to act “as quasi agents or forces with trajectories, propensities, or tendencies of their own” (Bennett, 2010, p. viii).

label: ethics of sustainability
definition: A transformative ethics including a critical or reactive and an affirmative or active phase.
source_quote: “an ethics of sustainability” structures her argument and that “this transformative ethics includes a critical or reactive and an affirmative or active phase” (Braidotti, 2006, p. 5).

label: autopoietic machine
definition: The subject as a self-producing machine fuelled by targeted perceptions, the echoing chamber of zoe.
source_quote: The subject is "an autopoietic machine fuelled by targeted perceptions" functioning as "the echoing chamber of zoe."

label: staying with the trouble
definition: the task Haraway names: cultivating the capacity to respond to worldly urgencies with each other
source_quote: she describes the task as “learning to stay with the trouble of living and dying in response-ability on a damaged earth” (Haraway, 2016, p. 2).

label: empirical-discursive methodological approach
definition: The approach bodily materialism produces, combining critique with the creation of alternatives.
source_quote: bodily materialism produces “a new empirical-discursive methodological approach that combines critique with the creation of alternatives” (Braidotti, 2024, p. xviii).

label: ouroboran
definition: Of concepts: living between the absolute and the human definition of knowing, looping on themselves.
source_quote: It is what Adorno names when he insists that concepts are ouroboran: all concepts live somewhere between the absolute and our more traditional human definition of knowing

label: the absolute
definition: The real, generating ground permanently beyond our grasp, between which and human knowing concepts live.
source_quote: concepts live somewhere between the absolute and our more traditional human definition of knowing, because the absolute is real, generating, and permanently beyond our grasp.

label: performative new materialism
definition: position anticipated by Lucretius: matter ceaselessly constitutes novel entities and relations
source_quote: Gamble, Hanan, and Nail argue that Lucretius anticipates performative new materialism by treating matter as something that ceaselessly constitutes novel entities and relations

label: reversibility
definition: the body as fold: not binary opposition between fixed terms but a relation that always miscarries at the last moment
source_quote: not binary opposition between two fixed terms, but a reversibility that always miscarries at the last moment (Coole, 2010, pp. 110–111)

label: dehiscence
definition: opening produced by the miscarrying reversibility, keeping emergence possible rather than inert repetition
source_quote: a reversibility that “always miscarries at the last moment,” producing the dehiscence through which emergence remains possible rather than closing into inert repetition (Coole, 2010, p. 107)

label: wild Being
definition: what Merleau-Ponty's notes apply Leibnizean concepts to once rid of substantialist, onto-theological elaborations
source_quote: only ridding them of their substantialist and onto-theological elaborations in order to apply them to wild Being

label: being-in-the-world
definition: term Merleau-Ponty's working notes planned to substitute for Leibniz's God
source_quote: His working notes  planned to substitute being-in-the-world for Leibniz's God

label: congruence
definition: one-to-one correspondence between signs and things; the classical representationalist demand Hayles replaces
source_quote: Congruence implies a one-to-one correspondence between signs and things — the classical representationalist demand that a representation mirror its object.

label: consistency
definition: Hayles's criterion replacing congruence: whether a representation is viable, holding at the cusp with the flux
source_quote: Consistency asks something different: not whether a representation accurately reflects reality, but whether it is viable

label: flux
definition: what constructed concepts can never fully capture; inherently unknowable and unreachable by any sentient being
source_quote: The flux is “inherently unknowable and unreachable by any sentient being” (Hayles [1991] 1997, cited in Timeto, 2011, p. 157)

label: cusp
definition: zone between constructed concepts and the flux where representations hold; the site where knowledge occurs
source_quote: whether it holds at the cusp between the constructed concepts through which we know the world and the flux that those concepts can never fully capture

label: refusal of closure
definition: preventing meaning from coming to closure at what is said or shown; kept open by the interval
source_quote: she argues that “meaning should be prevented from coming to closure at either what is said or what is shown”

label: resonance
definition: what dialogue between orders of knowledge amplifies, as against creating false equivalences
source_quote: “does not mean creating false equivalences” but instead “aims at amplifying possible resonances between them” (Braidotti, cited in Anderson, 2020, p. 205). The point here is not equivalence but resonance.

label: species-ism
definition: belligerent speciesism that, with Eurocentric universalism, produces exclusionary norms of the human
source_quote: Eurocentric universalism and belligerent “‘species-ism’” have produced exclusionary norms of the human

label: exceptionalist anthropocentrism
definition: object of the second intersecting critique, equated with anthropolatry; paired with critique of the man of reason
source_quote: the critique of the humanistic “‘man of reason’” and the critique of exceptionalist anthropocentrism, or “‘anthropolatry’” (Braidotti, 2024, p. xii)

label: bounded individualism
definition: what has finally become unavailable to think with across science, politics, and philosophy
source_quote: bounded individualism in its many flavors in science, politics, and philosophy has finally become unavailable to think with, truly no longer thinkable, technically or any other way

label: merely philosophical
definition: pejorative label that solidified a dismissive stance toward foundational interpretive questions in physics
source_quote: The label “merely philosophical” took on a pejorative tone and “solidified a dismissive stance toward the foundational issue. The foundational issues simply didn’t matter” (Barad, 2007, ch. 7)

label: ontic interpretation
definition: Barad's reading of Bohr: entities do not determinately exist apart from the apparatuses constituting them; vs epistemic readings
source_quote: her novel reading of Bohr as having advanced an ‘ontic’ interpretation against the ‘epistemic’ interpretations” of Schrödinger and Heisenberg (2019, p. 122)

label: self-denial of thought
definition: dogmatic denial of factors not expressible in a scheme's own primary notions; misuse of philosophic generalization
source_quote: producing “a dogmatic denial that there are any factors in the world not fully expressible in terms of its own primary notions devoid of further generalization” — what he calls “the self-denial of thought”

label: agentivity
definition: matter as active participant in the production of meaning, not passive substrate for human expression
source_quote: Rauschenberg’s practice is “especially sensitive to agentivity” (p. 258): matter appears not as passive substrate for human expression but as an active participant in the production of meaning

label: ontology of chance
definition: Deleuze's ontology in which Being is repeatedly constituted by events of chance, throws of the dice
source_quote: This “affirmative power of difference” is “the key principle of Deleuze’s ontology of chance” (Cheah, 2010, p. 82).

label: affirmative power of difference
definition: difference seen the right way up is affirmation, not negation; the key principle of Deleuze's ontology of chance
source_quote: Seen the right way up, from top to bottom, difference is affirmation. . . . It is not the negative which is the motor

label: dice throw
definition: Being constituted by throws of the dice that give rise to different singularities or commencements
source_quote: “Ontology is the dice throw, the chaosmos from which the cosmos emerges” (Cheah, 2010, p. 83).

label: clamor of Being
definition: the events of chance, taking the form of questions and imperatives, to which ideas or problems arise in response
source_quote: These events take the form of “questions and imperatives,” and ideas or problems arise in response to “this clamor of Being” (Cheah, 2010, p. 83).

label: actualization
definition: does not unfold a preformed possibility; determines a virtual field that is already real
source_quote: Actualization does not unfold a preformed possibility. It determines a virtual field that is already real (Cheah, 2010, pp. 84–85).

label: foundational comportments
definition: Bennett's trained orientations: willingness to suspend the preconceived; readiness to encounter thing-power
source_quote: Developing the capacity for relational perception requires what Bennett calls foundational comportments: an open-minded, open-ended willingness to suspend the preconceived

label: constitutive exclusions
definition: what the apparatus does not produce, as significant as what it does; the researcher is response-able for them
source_quote: exclusions are constitutive: what the apparatus does not produce is as significant as what it does, and the researcher is response-able for those constitutive exclusions (Barad, 2003; 2007)

label: experimenting with a diffractive apparatus
definition: happens within the event as an onto-epistemological material practice, unlike diffractive reading after the event
source_quote: diffractive reading usually happens after the event, while experimenting with a diffractive apparatus happens within the event as an “onto-epistemological material practice”

label: otherwise practice
definition: Lambert's framing of diffraction: not an either/or alternative to reflection but an expanded way of thinking
source_quote: diffraction is “not an ‘either/or’ alternative but an ‘otherwise’, expanded way of thinking” (p. 3)

label: ontological entanglements
definition: What transpositions as phenomena are; highly specific configurations that change with each intra-action
source_quote: She proposes "to understand transpositions—as phenomena—to be ontological entanglements" (Arlander, 2018, p. 43), following Barad's claim that entanglements are highly specific configurations

label: material continuum
definition: A continuum in which impurities, mixtures, and singularities resist categorization
source_quote: Kirschner extends this into artistic research through the language of a material continuum in which impurities, mixtures, and singularities resist categorization

label: critique
definition: A mode of disclosure, exposure and demystification, contrasted with diffractive reading's affirmative engagement

label: logic of representation
definition: A logic that remains singular across instances, distinguished from the logic of transposition

label: logic of transposition
definition: A logic that is "multiple," with "positional specificity" determined "in space, time, or otherwise"
source_quote: from "the logic of transposition," which is "multiple," with "positional specificity" determined "in space, time, or otherwise" (Schwab, 2018, pp. 7–8)

label: ontology of becoming
definition: The nature of all life is to become and keep doing so through embedded, embodied relations that produce affects

label: history tattooed on your body
definition: names the forms and experiences of oppression, empowerment, and difference constituting any specific location

label: embracing alternative ways of seeing and understanding the world
definition: First of six transpositions practices: reorienting before inquiry begins; deciding to see humanist dualisms at work
source_quote: Embracing alternative ways of seeing and understanding the world is a reorientation before inquiry begins.

label: assessing and critiquing imaginary formations
definition: Identifying the choreography of constraints and entitlements that imaginary forms materialize for historied bodies

label: preparing to make the creative leap
definition: Cultivating generative cross-pollinations across unconnected theoretical domains; embodying the nomad
source_quote: Preparing to make the creative leap: cultivating "generative cross-pollinations" across multiple and often seemingly unconnected theoretical domains, genres, modes of apprehension, and discursive communities

label: accounting for locations and positioning
definition: Attending to the embeddedness of historicity the researcher brings; a feminist politics of location in practice

label: storying the in-between space
definition: The work of experimentation and creation: storying more empowering rhythms for existing cultural formations
source_quote: accounting for locations and positioning, storying the in-between space, and developing new frames of resonance

label: possibility space
definition: the space opened by making things stranger, in which something new becomes thinkable
source_quote: making things stranger creates space to inhabit, space she claims as personal, as her own, the possibility space in which something new becomes thinkable (Andersen, 2016, p. 47)

label: attunement
definition: staying with the encounter the default frame cannot register; receptive orientation to the apparatus
source_quote: practicing what Bennett calls lingering and what Barad calls attunement to the apparatus, but from the inside: staying with the encounter that the default frame cannot register

label: anticipatory receptivity
definition: one of Bennett's named comportments, listed alongside lingering and openness
source_quote: as well as the comportments of lingering, openness, and anticipatory receptivity (Vibrant Matter, pp. 5, 16–18)

label: four Adornian techniques
definition: make conceptualization an object of thought; attend to qualitative singularities; utopian imagination; playful element

label: qualitative singularities
definition: the specific, irreducible ways a thing pushes back against the concept's flattening

label: clownish traits
definition: the playful element in inquiry: willing to present reality as apparent nonsense, to be wrong in public
source_quote: The fourth technique is to admit a playful element into inquiry: to be willing, as Adorno puts it, to adhere to one's "clownish traits."

label: logic of sense
definition: sense as pre-personal and pre-conscious, existing in the realm of potentialities

label: active material
definition: Material that actively affects the artist's touch and the emerging work; sets the pace of making or proposes otherwise
source_quote: The active material and the resistance it induces sets the pace for my art-making either by accepting work or by complicating it, but the material resistance may also stop my work altogether.

label: discipline of emergent processes
definition: Order replacing reductionism derived from control and hierarchical exercise of power in the fluid laboratory

label: handling
definition: Full multisensory engagement — touch, sounds, smells, texture, visions, tastes — preceding theory

label: performative moment
definition: The fog chamber in which ideas and devices prove themselves or fail; where thoughts are acted out

label: conversion of the artistic medium into a medium of research

label: transformative communication
definition: The transponent's mode of communication: not informative, not a medium; it changes the field it enters.

label: performative force

label: real magnitudes

label: from far to close (and back)

source_quote: becomes fertile ground for new empathetic technologies: technologies that facilitate a conversation on a specific research question

label: science-as-research

definition: Kant's move turning metaphysics into transcendental anthropology, starting philosophy with the human

definition: The ongoing process things emerge from and dissolve back into; traced by cartography, not mapped as fixed.
